title: Corrected Florida Current cable data show no 2004-2014 decline, so FC transport explains 0-17% (not 60%) of the South Florida sea-level acceleration; Gulf gauges rose similarly
abstract: Question: Park & Sweet (2015) reported a 3 Sv Florida Current (FC) decline from 2004 to 2014 and attributed about 60% of the 6-7 cm South Florida sea-level rise in that decade to it, with -1.4 cm/Sv. Volkov et al. (2024) found that the cable record after 2000 needed a geomagnetic correction. Approach: we compared the raw NCEI cable archive (1982-2022) and the corrected RAPID v2024.1a series (2004-2024) with 24 inverse-barometer-corrected NOAA tide gauges. Gulf-coast gauges were the controls. We fitted month-to-month coupling slopes on 1982-2014 and tested them on 2015-2024. Then we compared the decadal excess rise above the 1982-2002 rate with the FC-implied rise. Results: from 2003-05 to 2013-15, the FC change was -0.69 +/- 0.94 Sv (raw) and 0.00 +/- 1.04 Sv (corrected). EMD of the record to November 2014 gave a 1.6-2.6 Sv decline, but the record extended to 2016-2022 gave 0.55-0.94 Sv. Thus most of the published decline is an end-of-record effect. The fast coupling is real: Florida Straits and Southeast Atlantic gauges fell 0.6-1.8 cm per Sv, the slopes held out of sample (skill 0.14-0.43), the Bahamas side had the opposite sign, and Gulf gauges had none. At annual scale, the coupling was not resolved. The excess rise for 2004-2014 was 5.7-7.2 cm at Key West, Vaca Key and Virginia Key. The FC-implied rise was 0.97 cm with raw transport (13-17%) and 0.0 cm with corrected transport (95% bound below 27%). Gulf controls also rose 4.8 +/- 1.9 cm above their old rate. In 2014-2024, the Atlantic-minus-Gulf excess was negative, which is opposite to an FC cause. Our pre-registered rule rejects the FC attribution. Limitations: the annual-scale coupling slope has wide intervals, IB and wind data are coarse, and we did not reprocess the cable voltages.

display.caption: Excess decadal sea-level rise above the 1982-2002 rate (black) and FC-implied rise (raw cable x -1.4 cm/Sv, orange; corrected x -1.4, blue; corrected x fitted fast slope, aqua) for 2004-2014 and 2014-2024. Error bars are 95% intervals. The Gulf mean and the Atlantic-minus-Gulf bars show that the acceleration was regional and not FC-specific.

Annual Florida Current transport: raw NCEI cable archive (orange), corrected RAPID v2024.1a series (blue), and raw x Fz(2000)/Fz(t) only (aqua dashed, an overcorrection). Dotted lines: EMD low-frequency part for the record to November 2014 (orange) and to 2022 (grey). Lower panel: IGRF vertical field at the cable.

Month-to-month coupling slope (cm of sea level per Sv of FC) with 95% HAC intervals, fitted on 1982-2014 (orange) and 2015-2024 (blue). The dashed line is the -1.4 cm/Sv factor of Park & Sweet (2015).
